summary_paragraph: A male patient with cryptogenic cirrhosis was readmitted for worsening abdominal and flank pain, ascites, and confusion. He was found to have community-acquired pneumonia due to ciprofloxacin-resistant E. coli, hepatorenal syndrome, and hyponatremia. Despite maximal medical therapy, his liver and kidney function deteriorated, leading to evaluation for transplant. He underwent a successful orthotopic liver transplant but experienced postoperative complications including coagulopathy requiring massive transfusion, volume overload, and Enterococcus bacteremia. He was treated with antibiotics, immunosuppressants, and supportive care. His condition stabilized, and he was discharged to extended care for rehabilitation with a plan for close outpatient follow-up.
